big: Rohan and his wife hold a demat account jointly, with 'either or survivor'. When he passed away, she could continue on her own. A friend's family, with only one name on the account, needed months of paperwork.

lines: I named my brother as nominee. So everything is his?
Not always. A nominee is a person who receives the asset on death, but the final owner may be decided by the will or by law. That is why a will still matters.

intro: They sound alike, but they differ.
rows: Named to receive an asset, but not always its final owner
Shares an account, and in some modes the survivor continues
How the joint account is operated, such as either or survivor
Moving assets to heirs after death, once documents are given
note: Check the exact rules of each bank, fund house and depository. They can differ.

title: Nominee and joint holding
stops: A nominee receives it, but may not own it finally
Naming a nominee replaces the need for a will
In either or survivor, the survivor can carry on
caps: The will or the law can decide who finally owns it.
A will is still needed to say who should own what.
Either or survivor lets the other holder carry on after a death.
Heirs submit papers to the bank or fund house to move the assets.

q: Meena names her brother as nominee on a bank deposit. After her death, what is true?
opts: He is the final owner no matter what the will says
The bank keeps the whole deposit
He receives it, owner may differ
Her will is cancelled by this
why: A nominee is not always the final owner, so this is too strong.
A bank does not keep the money when there is a nominee or heir.
The nominee receives it, and the will or law sets the owner.
A nomination does not cancel a will in any way.

q: Rohan and his wife choose 'either or survivor' for a joint account. What does it allow?
opts: The survivor can keep operating it
Both must always sign every time
The account closes on one death
The bank decides who operates it
why: In this mode, the surviving holder can continue to hold and operate it.
That describes a stricter mode, where both must act together.
The account does not have to close when one holder passes away.
The holders choose the mode when the account is opened.

q: A fund house moves units to a legal heir after receiving papers. What is this called?
why: Renewal is continuing an insurance policy for another term.
Transmission is the process of moving assets to heirs after a death.
A premium is paid for insurance, and it is not redeemed.
Underinsurance means too low a sum insured.

q: Dadi has several accounts with no nominee. What is a wise step?
opts: Tell no one about the accounts
Close each of them at once
Add a nominee on each account
why: Hoping is not a plan, and the family may struggle to claim.
Telling no one keeps the accounts hidden when the family needs them.
Closing accounts is not needed, and it removes her savings from use.
A nominee gives a clear person to receive the asset and eases claims.

pts: A nominee receives an asset, but is not always its final owner.
Either or survivor lets the survivor keep operating a joint account.
Transmission moves assets to heirs once documents are given.
